01 / YOUR PRIVATE ACCOUNT

Unlocking requests the protocol’s “Privacy Money account sign in” message twice to verify consistent key recovery. This signature controls access to your private notes. Only sign it on trusted interfaces; never share it.

An inactive session locks even during a payment. A submitted transaction may still complete; check its status after unlocking.

Clear this wallet’s local history?

This deletes the saved activity list from this browser. Your funds, pool notes and onchain transactions are unchanged. These records cannot be restored here.

    Keep an encrypted backup.

    Move your saved history to another browser with the same wallet. This file does not back up your funds or private notes.

    Restore this history backup?

    Existing records are kept. New restored transaction statuses need a fresh network check.

    The latest 100 activities are kept here. No history is sent to an analytics backend. Status checks contact your selected RPC; explorer links open a third-party service. About local history ↗

    04 / SHARE A REQUEST

    Request a payment.

    Create a link or QR code for a SOL or USDC payment. The recipient address is public.

    Anyone with the link can read the address and amount. The payer reviews fees and confirms separately. A request does not prove payment.

    No checks have run yet.

    Availability is a point-in-time check, not a security audit or a promise that a payment will succeed. Checks send read requests to your RPC and Privacy Cash.

    Recover with the same wallet.

    Keep access to the original software wallet. The same protocol message must reproduce the same signature. Hardware wallets are unsupported by this SDK.

    Proofs stay on this device.

    Hushmark generates the protocol proof locally. Encrypted notes are fetched from Privacy Cash; withdrawal proofs go to its relayer.

    Privacy has limits.

    Timing, matching amounts, address reuse and service metadata can reduce privacy. Avoid sending back to the funding wallet.
